5. Moving Money Between Your Rho-Bank Accounts
   ID: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_022
   Score: 15.0804
   Content: One of the many conveniences of being a Rho-Bank customer is the ability to easily move money between your accounts. Whether you're transferring funds from your checking account to your savings account to build up your emergency fund, moving money from savings to checking to cover an upcoming expense, or simply reorganizing your finances across multiple accounts, Rho-Bank makes it simple and straightforward.

## Self-Service Options

The fastest way to transfer money between your Rho-Bank accounts is through our digital banking platforms. Using the Rho-Bank mobile app or online banking at rhobank.com, you can initiate transfers instantly, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Simply log in, navigate to the transfer section, select your source and destination accounts, enter the amount, and confirm. It's that easy, and there's no fee for transferring money between your own Rho-Bank accounts.

## Need Assistance? We're Here to Help

If you prefer to have a customer service representative handle the transfer for you, or if you're having any trouble with the digital platforms, our team is happy to assist. Simply call us at 1-800-RHO-BANK or chat with us through the mobile app, and we can process the transfer on your behalf. This can be especially convenient if you're setting up a new savings account and want us to transfer the opening deposit from your checking account, or if you need to consolidate balances across multiple accounts.

## A Few Things to Keep in Mind

Both the source account (where the money is coming from) and the destination account (where the money is going) must be open and in good standing. The source account must have sufficient funds to cover the transfer amount—if the balance is too low, the transfer won't go through. Internal transfers between your own Rho-Bank accounts are always free of charge.

7. Internal: Freezing and Unfreezing a Debit Card
   ID: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026
   Score: 15.0074
   Content: Procedure for when a customer wants to temporarily freeze or unfreeze their debit card.

## Freezing vs. Closing

- FREEZE: Temporary lock - card can be unfrozen later. Use when customer misplaced the card or wants temporary security.
- CLOSE: Permanent deactivation - cannot be reversed. Use when card is confirmed lost/stolen or customer wants to cancel.

## Reasons for Freezing

- Customer misplaced the card and is looking for it
- Traveling and wants extra security
- Suspicious activity noticed, wants to investigate before closing
- Temporarily restricting spending (e.g., budgeting purposes)
- Lending card to family member and wants to control usage

## Freezing Requirements

1. Customer must be verified
2. Customer must be the owner of the debit card
3. Card must currently be in ACTIVE status (cannot freeze PENDING, CLOSED, or already FROZEN cards)

## Freezing Steps

1. Verify customer identity
2. Ask customer why they want to freeze the card
3. Inform customer of the following:
   - All new transactions will be declined while frozen
   - Recurring payments/subscriptions will also be declined
   - Pending transactions already authorized may still process
   - They can unfreeze at any time by calling customer service or through the mobile app
4. Use freeze_debit_card_3892 with the card_id
5. Confirm the freeze was successful

## Unfreezing Requirements

1. Customer must be verified
2. Customer must be the owner of the debit card
3. Card must currently be in FROZEN status
4. The linked checking account must still be OPEN

## Unfreezing Steps

1. Verify customer identity
2. Use unfreeze_debit_card_3893 with the card_id
3. Confirm the card is now active and ready to use immediately

## Important Notes

- Freezing does not affect ATM access if the customer has their PIN
- For ATM freeze, customer must also enable 'ATM Block' separately through mobile app
- If a frozen card is not unfrozen within 90 days, the customer will receive a reminder notification
- If customer confirms the card is lost/stolen, recommend closing instead of freezing

8. Silver Rewards Card: Understanding Your Included Travel Insurance Coverage
   ID: doc_credit_cards_silver_rewards_card_005

   Content: ## Coverage Overview
- Per-trip coverage limit: up to $15,000
- Covered incident types: up to 5 categories (for example, trip cancellation or interruption, delays, lost or delayed baggage, or similar covered events)

## Key Eligibility Conditions
- Charge the covered travel fare in full to your card for coverage to apply
- Coverage applies per trip and is subject to policy terms, exclusions, and documentation requirements

## What Is Typically Covered
- Non-refundable, prepaid travel expenses when a covered event occurs
- Essential items during eligible baggage delay
- Reasonable additional costs due to covered delays

## What Is Typically Not Covered
- Known events or foreseen issues at the time of booking
- Non-covered reasons for cancellation or changes
- Losses without required documentation (e.g., carrier delay notices, receipts)

## How Benefits Are Applied
- Reimbursements are capped per trip at $15,000 and depend on the specific covered incident type among the up to 5 categories
- Benefits may be secondary to other applicable coverage you hold

## Proof You Should Keep
- Original itineraries and tickets
- Receipts for additional expenses
- Official delay/cancellation notices or property irregularity reports (for baggage issues)

9. Spending Alerts and Budget Controls on Hunter Green
   ID: doc_business_checking_accounts_hunter_green_005
   Score: 14.5555
   Content: ## Defaults at a glance
- Real-time spending alerts are enabled by default: Yes.
- The default alert threshold is $100. You will receive an alert when a single transaction meets or exceeds this amount.
- A spending limit buffer of $2,000 allows limited flexibility above your available balance for transactions.

## Customizing alerts
- Adjust your alert threshold above or below $100 to match your typical transaction sizes.
- Enable alerts for card-present, online, or international transactions based on your risk tolerance.
- Set delivery preferences for push or email notifications so you see alerts in time to act.

## Understanding the spending limit buffer
- Transactions within the $2,000 buffer may be approved even when your available balance is temporarily insufficient.
- Use alerts to immediately review and reconcile any buffered transactions so your balance aligns with expected activity.

## Best practices
- Calibrate the threshold near your average invoice or purchase size so meaningful alerts are surfaced.
- If you anticipate larger purchases, temporarily raise the threshold and then reset it after the transaction clears.

10. Gold Rewards Card: No Foreign Transaction Fees - International Purchases Made Easy
   ID: doc_credit_cards_gold_rewards_card_004
   Score: 14.5448
   Content: ## Your Fee on International Purchases
- Foreign transaction fee charged by Rho‑Bank on this card: 0%

## What Counts as an International Purchase
- In‑person transactions at merchants outside your home country
- Online purchases processed by a merchant whose acquiring bank or payment gateway is located abroad
- Subscriptions billed by international entities, even if priced in your home currency

## Currency Conversion Considerations
- Some merchants may offer dynamic currency conversion at checkout. Choosing local currency can yield better rates, but you should compare the total before confirming.
- Network exchange rates and any merchant‑applied conversion charges are separate from Rho‑Bank’s foreign transaction fee of 0%.

## Tips for Smooth International Use
- Enable travel notifications if your risk controls require it.
- Keep a backup payment method for locations with connectivity or network constraints.
- Retain receipts for any disputed charges and contact support promptly with details.
